meta.title_plain: How to make your money grow on its own
meta.teaser: Learn how saved money earns more money, and why starting early is a superpower.

page.title: How to make your money grow on its own
page.sub: A skill you can use today
page.bigIdea: Saved money can earn its own money. With compound interest, time is your superpower, so the earlier you start, the more it grows.

cards.title: Know principal and interest
cards.front: Why would a bank pay you just for saving?
cards.back: Principal is the money you start with. Interest is extra money paid for keeping it saved. Simple interest pays only on that starting pile.
cards.tryit: Ask Dad what interest rate a kids' savings account pays here. Write the number down.

cards.title: Interest earns interest too
cards.front: What happens when your interest starts working for you?
cards.back: $1,000 at 5% becomes $1,050 after one year. Year two pays 5% on $1,050, giving $1,102.50. That's compound interest: it snowballs, like a level-up that boosts your next level-up.
cards.tryit: On a calculator, type 100, then keep multiplying by 1.1. How many presses until it passes 200?

cards.title: Use the Rule of 72
cards.front: A quick brain trick to see how fast money doubles.
cards.back: Divide 72 by the interest rate to estimate the years to double. At 9%, $100 becomes $200 in about 8 years. Luca Pacioli wrote this rule in 1494.
cards.tryit: Use the Rule of 72 for 3%, 6% and 12%. Which one doubles fastest?

cards.title: Ben Franklin's 100-year plan
cards.front: A famous inventor tested compound interest after he died.
cards.back: In 1789, Franklin's will gave £1,000 each to Boston and Philadelphia, lent out at 5%. He predicted each would grow to £131,000 after 100 years.
cards.tryit: Multiply 1,000 by 1.05 ten times on a calculator. How much after 10 years?

cards.title: Start early, add often
cards.front: Why does a 13-year-old saver have a head start?
cards.back: $100 at 6% doubles about every 12 years. Save it at 13, and by 61 it's about $1,600. Wait until 25, and it's only about $800.
cards.tryit: Pick a goal. Decide one small amount you could save every week from gifts or chores.

words.d: The money you put in at the start.
Extra money paid to you for keeping your money saved.
The percent of your money you earn as interest each year.
Interest paid on your money plus the interest it already earned.
Divide 72 by the rate to guess how long money takes to double.

quiz.q: You save $100 at 10% compound interest per year. How much after 2 years?
quiz.hint: Work one year at a time. What is year two's 10% taken from?
quiz.why: Year one gives $110, then year two pays 10% of $110, which is $11, so $121.

quiz.q: Using the Rule of 72, about how long does money take to double at 6%?
quiz.hint: The rule has just one step. Which two numbers do you divide?
quiz.why: 72 divided by 6 is 12, so it takes about 12 years to double.

quiz.q: What makes compound interest different from simple interest?
opts: It only pays once, at the very end
It needs a bank card to work
It pays interest on earlier interest too
quiz.hint: Think of the snowball. What gets added to the pile each year?
quiz.why: Compound interest adds earned interest to the pile, so the next interest is bigger.

quiz.q: Maya saves $100 at 13. Leo saves $100 at 25. Both earn 6%. Who has more at 61?
opts: Leo, because he saved when older
Maya, because her money had time to double once more
quiz.hint: Count the years each person's money grows. How many 12-year doubles fit?
quiz.why: Maya's money grows 48 years (4 doubles) and Leo's 36 years (3 doubles), so Maya wins.

page.think: Plan your own savings goal. What would you save for, how much could you add each week, and how long would it take to get there?
